title: Break the Receptor, Add the Ligand

scenes.tts: Break one signaling receptor in a frog cell, without adding anything new. What will an animal cap become?
scenes.visual: Title card: Break the Receptor, Add the Ligand. An animal cap in a dish with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Break one signaling receptor in a frog cell, without adding anything new. What will an animal cap become?

scenes.tts: Every experiment here uses the same tissue, the animal cap, cultured in salt solution.
scenes.visual: The blastula map: a hollow ball of cells drawn in cross-section, animal cap at the top shaded as ectoderm, blastocoel inside, endoderm at the floor; beside it a gastrula with the blastopore groove on the lower half, its dorsal lip labeled organizer, dorsal and ventral arrows. The cap is cut out and moved into a dish.
scenes.narration: Every experiment here uses the same tissue, the animal cap, cultured in salt solution.

scenes.tts: Left intact, it becomes epidermis and makes epidermal keratin. That is the control.
scenes.visual: The intact cap turns grey, the color for keratin. Label: control, epidermis.
scenes.narration: Left intact, it becomes epidermis and makes epidermal keratin. That is the control.

scenes.tts: B M Ps signal through pairs of receptor kinases, a type two and a type one.
scenes.caption: BMPs signal through pairs of receptor kinases, a type II and a type I.
scenes.visual: A BMP dimer binds two receptor types spanning the membrane. Labels: type II, type I.
scenes.narration: BMPs signal through pairs of receptor kinases, a type II and a type I.

scenes.tts: The type one receptor phosphorylates Smad one, five or eight. It moves to the nucleus with Smad four.
scenes.caption: The type I receptor phosphorylates Smad1, 5 or 8. It moves to the nucleus with Smad4.
scenes.visual: The type I receptor adds a phosphate to a Smad; Smad1 with Smad4 enters the nucleus and target genes light.
scenes.narration: The type I receptor phosphorylates Smad1, 5 or 8. It moves to the nucleus with Smad4.

scenes.tts: Now remove one receptor's kinase domain. It still binds ligand and still pairs with normal partners.
scenes.visual: One receptor loses its inner kinase domain but still binds ligand and pairs with a normal partner.
scenes.narration: Now remove one receptor's kinase domain. It still binds ligand and still pairs with normal partners.

scenes.tts: But it cannot pass the signal on, so it jams the complexes it joins.
scenes.visual: The complex with the broken receptor stays dark; no Smad is phosphorylated.
scenes.narration: But it cannot pass the signal on, so it jams the complexes it joins.

scenes.tts: This is a dominant negative: a broken copy that blocks the working copies.
scenes.visual: Label: dominant negative, a broken copy that blocks the working copies.
scenes.narration: This is a dominant negative: a broken copy that blocks the working copies.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-four, Ali Hemmati-Brivanlou and Douglas Melton injected eggs with R N A for such a receptor.
scenes.caption: In 1994, Ali Hemmati-Brivanlou and Douglas Melton injected eggs with RNA for such a receptor.
scenes.visual: Label: 1994, Hemmati-Brivanlou and Melton. A needle injects RNA into a frog egg.
scenes.narration: In 1994, Ali Hemmati-Brivanlou and Douglas Melton injected eggs with RNA for such a receptor.

scenes.tts: It was built from an activin receptor. But it also blocks signaling by related ligands.
scenes.visual: Label: built from an activin receptor; also blocks related ligands.
scenes.narration: It was built from an activin receptor. But it also blocks signaling by related ligands.

scenes.tts: Cut caps from the injected embryos and culture them alone. What do they become?
scenes.visual: Caps from injected embryos sit alone in dishes. Question on screen: what do they become?
scenes.narration: Cut caps from the injected embryos and culture them alone. What do they become?

scenes.tts: Neural tissue, with no mesoderm detected that could have induced it.
scenes.visual: The caps turn blue, the color for neural genes. Label: neural; no mesoderm detected.
scenes.narration: Neural tissue, with no mesoderm detected that could have induced it.

scenes.tts: Blocking a receptor, not adding a signal, made neural tissue.
scenes.visual: Text on screen: blocking a receptor, not adding a signal, made neural tissue.
scenes.narration: Blocking a receptor, not adding a signal, made neural tissue.

scenes.tts: Which blocked signal normally keeps ectoderm as skin? The receptor blocks activin, and related signals too. But activin added to caps makes mesoderm, not skin.
scenes.visual: The broken receptor shown blocking activin and a related ligand. Then a cap given activin turns into mesoderm, not grey skin. Label: activin makes mesoderm, a poor candidate for the skin signal.
scenes.narration: Which blocked signal normally keeps ectoderm as skin? The receptor blocks activin, and related signals too. But activin added to caps makes mesoderm, not skin.

scenes.tts: A relative fit better: B M P four. Its R N A is in the ectoderm early.
scenes.caption: A relative fit better: BMP4. Its RNA is in the ectoderm early.
scenes.visual: BMP4 RNA shown as dots throughout the early ectoderm. Label: BMP4.
scenes.narration: A relative fit better: BMP4. Its RNA is in the ectoderm early.

scenes.tts: And it is cleared from the dorsal side as the neural plate appears.
scenes.visual: The dots fade from the dorsal side as a neural plate outline forms there.
scenes.narration: And it is cleared from the dorsal side as the neural plate appears.

scenes.tts: To test B M P four directly, you need cap cells that would otherwise turn neural.
scenes.caption: To test BMP4 directly, you need cap cells that would otherwise turn neural.
scenes.visual: A dish of cap cells. Label: need cells that would otherwise turn neural.
scenes.narration: To test BMP4 directly, you need cap cells that would otherwise turn neural.

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-nine, Horst Grunz and Lothar Tacke had found them.
scenes.caption: In 1989, Horst Grunz and Lothar Tacke had found them.
scenes.visual: Label: 1989, Grunz and Tacke.
scenes.narration: In 1989, Horst Grunz and Lothar Tacke had found them.

scenes.tts: They separated cap cells in medium lacking the calcium and magnesium the cells need to stick together.
scenes.visual: A cap falls apart into scattered single cells in a dish. Label: no calcium, no magnesium.
scenes.narration: They separated cap cells in medium lacking the calcium and magnesium the cells need to stick together.

scenes.tts: They kept the cells apart for hours, then let them clump again. The cells made neural tissue.
scenes.visual: A clock runs for hours; the cells clump again and turn blue. Label: separated cells, neural.
scenes.narration: They kept the cells apart for hours, then let them clump again. The cells made neural tissue.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-five, Paul Wilson and Hemmati-Brivanlou separated cap cells the same way and added B M P four protein.
scenes.caption: In 1995, Paul Wilson and Hemmati-Brivanlou separated cap cells the same way and added BMP4 protein.
scenes.visual: Label: 1995, Wilson and Hemmati-Brivanlou. Scattered cells with BMP4 dimers added to the medium.
scenes.narration: In 1995, Paul Wilson and Hemmati-Brivanlou separated cap cells the same way and added BMP4 protein.

scenes.tts: What do these cells become?
scenes.visual: Question on screen: separated cells plus BMP4, what do they become?
scenes.narration: What do these cells become?

scenes.tts: Epidermis. Their neural genes stayed off. The ligand alone was enough to restore skin.
scenes.visual: The cells turn grey. Label: epidermis; neural genes off.
scenes.narration: Epidermis. Their neural genes stayed off. The ligand alone was enough to restore skin.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: jam the receptor and a cap turns neural. Add B M P four back and separated cells return to skin.
scenes.caption: The takeaway: jam the receptor and a cap turns neural. Add BMP4 back and separated cells return to skin.
scenes.visual: Two dishes side by side: a blue jammed-receptor cap and grey BMP4-treated cells. Takeaway on screen.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: jam the receptor and a cap turns neural. Add BMP4 back and separated cells return to skin.
